text:
harper: Heads up — hit a weird onboarding issue in examples/python-starter. Structured JSON logs include request payloads and our redactor isn't catching the api_key field when it's nested.

eno: ouch. nested JSON? can you paste sample log and env?

harper: raw line: `2026-11-03T12:04:11Z INFO {"path":"/chat","user":{"email":"u@example.com","credentials":{"api_key":"sk_live_ABC123SECRET"}},"request_id":null}`

sylvie: aha — our redactor runs a regex on the raw log string before json-parsing in the python sample, but when logs are emitted as structured dicts (logger.json(...)) the logger bypasses string path and the redact hook runs after serialization in a different order. result: json-encoded value stays intact.

eno: how is OTEL involved?

harper: when OTEL_LOG_INJECTION=true, the otel hook serializes trace fields into the structured payload after our redactor step so the redacter also runs against the serialized payload but only does a simple string replace that assumes token appears as plaintext (not quoted inside JSON). our current regex expects bare tokens like `sk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}` but inside JSON it's `"sk_live_..."` which still matches, however header-like tokens in nested objects used different characters and are Base64-encoded in some integrations, so they don't match.

sylvie: hmm. two separate issues: 1) order of ops between our redact hook and otel injection (fields added after redaction), 2) our redactor is not operating on parsed JSON fields and misses nested keys or encoded values.

mina: quick mitigation: make redactor JSON-aware in python SDK: walk dicts and redact values by key and regex, not just run global string replace. also ensure redact runs after OTEL injection or make it idempotent and safe to run multiple times.

eno: agree. parity note: Go and Node SDKs have dict-aware redactors; Python was historically string-path first. let's make parity change.

harper: also noticed request_id is null on first logs in python-starter when the builtin retry/backoff wraps the request. Node and Go generate op IDs differently — parity gap. in python retry middleware we clone the request context which resets `request_id` to None if not explicit.

sylvie: solution: retain an `operation_id` on the outer request context and emit `attempt_id` for retries. also fix middleware to inherit operation_id if present.

mina: for immediate prod safety, suggest adding a CI smoke test in examples/python-starter: start sample with `OTEL_LOG_INJECTION=true` and `REDWOOD_REDACT_PATTERNS='sk_live_'`, perform a request that includes nested api_key, then assert logs contain no `sk_live_` substrings. fail CI if any found.

eno: and add unit tests for redaction: (a) dict walk redactor, (b) double-pass idempotency, (c) base64 decode attempt for header-like tokens (best-effort).

harper: i'll open a PR that: 1) makes python redactor parse dicts and recurse, 2) ensures redact runs after otel injection (or is idempotent), 3) fixes retry middleware to preserve operation_id + emit attempt_id, 4) adds the CI smoke test and docs note.

sylvie: can you also include a small sample in examples/python-starter/tests/repro that shows the nested case? saves reviewers time.

harper: yep. PR draft in 30m.

redwood-bot: NOTE: created issue #4933 (devex) "python-starter: structured JSON logs miss nested api_key redaction; reqid parity with retries" by harper

mina: small follow-up: consider a global redact pass that runs on final serialized output in the collector as last-resort — makes sure nothing leaks even if SDK redaction misses. but that's a heavier hammer.

eno: good idea for defense-in-depth. let's prioritize SDK fix first.

harper: thanks all. ping me for reviews. :shipit:
